audit.whatIsWrong: The page tells the player Counter Strike dodges the empowered W stun ('activate to dodge your empowered W stun and flip the exchange', 'it dodges your E auto-follow'). Counter Strike dodges incoming basic attacks — Ruthless Predator is a spell and lands through it, stun included. The real rule is the opposite of what the page says: cast W and Q into the dodge, and hold your autos until it ends. Counter Strike's 17s rank-1 cooldown was never given either.
audit.why: Jax E: 'dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack, stunning all surrounding enemies', 17/15/13/11/9. Renekton W is an ability, not a basic attack.
audit.corrected: Stated in dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, dontsFull[0].d, whys[2] and wants.foe[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows gave Renekton the lane while the whys underneath give it to Jax from level 3: whys[2] 'flipping the pattern you depend on', whys[3] 'Jax wins Levels 4-5', whys[4] 'wins every duel', whys[6] 'wins every extended 1v1 decisively'. The page also presented it as a favoured lane — green tone, 4/10 difficulty, Ignite to 'convert the favoured lane' — against a 49.51% win rate and a 10/10 carry threat.
audit.why: Packet chart is Renekton, Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax; the mirror flipped rows 1-6 to the same shape and set its own side to EVEN at 5.5/10.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-6 flipped in matched pairs with ratings 5/4/4/3/3/2; diffRating to 6/10, tone to the even amber, and the difficulty, final-rating and summoner lines brought in line.

audit.whatIsWrong: The First-item row credited your Eclipse; spikes[3] says Trinity Force's Spellblade on every Leap Strike is what owns that window.
audit.why: Jax's curve runs through Trinity Force into Rageblade while Relentless Assault stacks attack speed on consecutive autos.
audit.corrected: phases[2].why, phases[3].why, phases[5].why and phases[6].why rewritten to the real order with Counter Strike's cooldown as the trigger.

audit.why: Packet flagged 'Bait Counter Strike' and 'Hold Counter Strike' as probable wrong names; Counter Strike is the correct name and both are false positives from the leading verb.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Counter Strike and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Counter Strike and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Jax carry threat 10/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Jax carry threat 10/10.

edits.before: Flash + Ignite — convert the favoured lane into kills.
edits.after: Flash + Teleport; Ignite only to force the early window.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Jax must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Counter Strike online at 3 — your autos feed the dodge and his counter-stun follows, so the pattern flips to him.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Counter Strike's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: He wins short Counter Strike trades from here — its 17s at rank 1 is your only window, and Relentless Assault out-stacks you.

edits.before: Eclipse is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Counter Strike's cooldown.
edits.after: His Trinity Force beats your Eclipse — Spellblade on every Leap Strike outdoes your burst.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Jax carry threat 10/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Rageblade Jax wins any extended 1v1 — split for pressure and fight only in short bursts on a spent Counter Strike.

edits.before: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: It dodges basic attacks only — your W stun lands through it. 17s at rank 1.

edits.before: Track Jax's Counter Strike: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. When it is down — W-stun + Q him.
edits.after: Counter Strike dodges basic attacks, not spells — your W still stuns him; hold autos until it ends.

edits.before: That is Jax's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Every auto into the dodge is wasted — Q and W still land, so cast those.

edits.before: Counter Strike is live at level 3 — it dodges your E auto-follow and stuns you after, flipping the pattern you depend on to win trades.
edits.after: Counter Strike is live at level 3 — it eats every basic attack you throw after the stun and counter-stuns you, flipping your trade pattern.

edits.before: Hold Counter Strike until your E commits, then activate to dodge your empowered W stun and flip the exchange
edits.after: Hold Counter Strike until you commit, eat the stun, then counter-stun you while your follow-up autos hit the dodge

notes: The dodge error is the one that actually cost games: the page had players hold their W for a window that does not exist, when the correct play is to cast W and Q into Counter Strike and withhold only the autos. Chart proposed as one atomic group. I also moved the favoured-lane framing (green tone, 4/10, Ignite line) to even, matching the mirror's 5.5/10 EVEN on the Jax side and the 49.51% win rate; if the user prefers page-scale labels left alone, those four edits are the ones to drop.
